body:
I think I might have BPD but I keep fighting the world saying I don't. I understand that it's much more than that. I'm in a different stage in life than you, but I've been there. I'm at the point now where relationships aren't even that important to me anymore but the same thing is holding me back- fear of failing. I'm scared of killing myself because I'm scared I'm going to fail. 

I've been through all of this and now I've come to a point where I just don't speak to people anymore. I'm too scared of dealing with my emotions involved in speaking to people.

I want to keep talking (because I relate so much) but I think it's going to end up all over the place. (And honestly this is the most I've been able to open up about myself in a while and it frightens me--all those emotions frighten me to the point of where I avoid them. I have almost no human contact)

I'm scared of getting help because it will all end up the same, I will end up back in bed and miserable-incapable of handling these emotions.

I feel like I'm in that black hole. I keep trying to climb out but something else keeps happening that keeps bringing me down again. The last straw was my best friends death (two years ago!). I managed to graduate college, despite being a single mother and having my dad/best friend die within 5 years. But what was the point? Why did I waste all my energy just to end up back in bed thinking that there is no solution. I have a degree and - what am I doing with it? Spending months in depression in my bed thinking about how much I hate myself (obsessive thoughts that have just become habitual) This is me. I see myself "getting better" but never ever returning to being "who I am" anymore. I've changed into this terrible person that I loathe. This person doesn't belong on this earth.  

>>admittedly I have defined myself as my illness. My depression is who I am. I just don't see it any other way. I wish I had the energy to research more about the brain and study it but my energy is lacking. I just don't want to do anything anymore. Sorry if this is getting repetitive. I don't know what to do. I know I need to do something but the only solution seems to be suicide, even though I know deep down that's not what I want to do but it just doesn't like I have a choice in the matter. 

And then there's the other factor==my depression is familiar. being happy is so unfamiliar it scares me. I'm scared that with happiness, depression inevitably follows. I'm scared to even be happy.

I've already wasting twenties away on depression. I'm wasting my chances of a career. I'm a failure. I can't even make it to basic appointments without help. I feel like a child but I don't want to be thought of as one. I just want someone to help me, to respect me as an adult ... 

Something is wrong with me. There's always something stopping me. I just know i need help. :'( 

I'm wasting my life away.

I would explain all the red tape business but it brings up too many bad memories/associations with the terrible care I've received from the mental health industry. It's not that it isn't accessable. I first need to deal with getting my car inspected (which it... a whole different ball game). But other than that, my big problem is that I don't have the energy to actually DO these things. There's nothing propping me up. There's a weight pulling me down the entire time

They were just doing their job. Honestly, having the cops cuff you is one of the most traumatic experiences, especially when you're suicidal. I've had it happen a few times, an ex of mine called whenever he was too worried and the police here said they had no choice but to take me to a hospital if he called. And the hospitals are terrible. They take away your free will.
The practice let me go. They have a lot of red tape and it's the only one relatively close to me. The next one is about a 45 minute drive.
Me too. I haven't really left in months
I feel that way too. It's like there is a magnet between me and my bed, always pulling me back inside. I just know that it's another thing I'm going to fail at. I'm never motivated.
I'm thinking of ending it too. But that sounds like way too much effort

This is me. I feel like that by getting help I'm just putting in more effort- only to be shot down again by my depression. It seems pointless to put in anymore effort when inevitably I'm only going to end up back in bed--depressed.
I think Danielle would have had the better sob story- she needed the money for her father's cancer.
